breakdown.description: A transient heat equation is written while the problem is described as steady with no time dependence (equations/assumptions conflict).
breakdown.reason: The agent recognized the conflict between the transient equation (dT/dt = α d²T/dx²) and the steady-state description. It explicitly resolved this by stating 'Set the time derivative in the heat equation dT/dt = α d²T/dx² to zero to obtain the steady-state form,' which yields d²T/dx² = 0 — matching the ground truth's guidance that for steady conduction one should 'set d²T/dx²=0 and remove the time derivative.' The agent did not blindly repeat the contradictory instructions.
